questions.title: Styles
questions.text: Describe what a **style** is in a word processor.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A named set of formatting (font, size, colour, spacing) e.g. Heading 1 (1)
- applied in one click; changing the style updates all text that uses it (1)
scheme.model_answer: A style is a named set of formatting, such as Heading 1, that can be applied with one click; if the style is changed, all text using it changes too.

questions.title: Why heading styles
questions.text: Explain why a programmer should use heading styles in a 60-page technical document.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): consistent headings; change all headings at once; automatic table of contents; navigation pane; chapter titles in headers (StyleRef); automatic heading numbering
scheme.model_answer: All headings look the same and can be changed at once, and an automatic table of contents can be created from them.

questions.title: Table of contents
questions.text:
Complete the sentences.

An automatic table of contents is created from text formatted with [[1]] styles. It is inserted from the [[2]] tab. After the document is edited, the contents is corrected by choosing [[3]] Table.

scheme.mark_scheme: (1) heading (2) References (3) Update

questions.title: Page break
questions.text: Pressing Enter many times is the best way to start a new chapter on a new page.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: A page break keeps the chapter on a new page even when text above it changes; empty lines move.

questions.title: Section breaks
questions.text: A report contains a wide ERD that must be printed on a **landscape** page, while the other pages are **portrait**. Explain how this can be done.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Insert a section break (next page) before and after the ERD page (1)
- set that section's orientation to landscape (the others stay portrait) (1)
scheme.model_answer: Put section breaks before and after the ERD so it is in its own section, then change only that section's orientation to landscape.

questions.title: Header and footer tools
questions.text: Match each header/footer tool to its effect.

left.text: Page number format i, ii, iii

right.text: No header on the title page
A section can have its own header text
Shows the total number of pages, as in Page 5 of 40
Roman numerals for the contents pages

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3, L4–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Fields
questions.text: Select **two** items that can be inserted in a footer as **fields** that update automatically.

scheme.mark_scheme: A and C. One mark each; a mark is lost for each incorrect option selected.

questions.title: Footnote options
questions.text: State **two** options that can be changed in the footnote settings of a word processor.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): location (bottom of page / below text / end of document / section); number format (1, a, i, symbols); start at; numbering continuous / restart each section / page; convert to endnotes
scheme.model_answer: 1 The number format, for example 1, 2, 3 or a, b, c. 2 Restarting the numbering in each section.

questions.title: Footnote settings
questions.text: Tick (✓) the setting needed for each requirement.

prefill: Each chapter's footnotes should start again from 1
All notes should be moved to the end of the report

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Number format (1); 2 Numbering restart (1); 3 Convert to endnotes (1)

questions.title: Write a footnote
questions.text: In the analysis section, a student writes: *"The library lends about 300 books every week."* The figure came from an interview with the head librarian, Mrs Ospanova, on 3 October 2026. Write a suitable footnote and state where the reference mark should go.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Footnote giving the source: interview with Mrs Ospanova, head librarian, 03.10.2026 (1)
- reference mark after the sentence / after the full stop following "week" (1)
scheme.model_answer: Reference mark after "week." — footnote: ¹ Interview with Mrs Ospanova, head librarian, 3 October 2026.

questions.title: Automatic footnotes
questions.text: Explain why footnotes should be inserted with the **Insert Footnote** tool rather than by typing numbers and notes at the bottom of the page.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): numbering is automatic / renumbers when notes are added or deleted; the note stays on the same page as its mark when text moves; consistent formatting (Footnote Text style); can be converted to endnotes
scheme.model_answer: The footnotes are renumbered automatically when one is added, and each note moves with its reference mark when the text changes, so it always stays on the right page.

questions.title: Table tools
questions.text: Match each table tool to its purpose.

right.text: Column headings appear at the top of each page of a long table
Alternate rows are shaded so they are easy to follow
All tables get the same borders, shading and fonts

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3, L4–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Captions
questions.text: Explain the advantage of adding table captions with **Insert Caption** rather than typing them.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Captions are numbered automatically and renumbered when tables are added / removed (1)
- a list of tables / table of figures and cross-references can be created and updated (1)
scheme.model_answer: The tables are numbered automatically and renumbered when a new table is inserted, and a list of all tables can be generated from the captions.

questions.title: Cross-references
questions.text: The text says *"see Table 4 on page 17"*. A new table is added earlier in the document. Explain why the reference should be made with the **Cross-reference** tool.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- The table becomes Table 5 / moves to another page (1)
- a cross-reference is a field that updates the number and page automatically; typed text would be wrong (1)
scheme.model_answer: After the new table, Table 4 becomes Table 5 and may move to page 18; a cross-reference updates automatically, whereas typed text would now be wrong.

questions.title: Rows across pages
questions.text: For a test-plan table it is good practice to stop a single row from being split across two pages.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.

questions.title: Format a project report
questions.text:
A team of three students writes one 50-page project report. Each student formats headings differently, the contents page was typed by hand and is now wrong, and the test-plan table is split over four pages without headings on the later pages.

Suggest how the team should use the word processor's tools to fix these problems. Justify each suggestion.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Up to 4 marks:
- Agree / apply heading styles — consistent formatting across authors (1)
- Automatic table of contents from the heading styles, updated after editing (1)
- Repeat header rows in the test-plan table so headings appear on every page (1)
- Table style / caption / rows not split / page-number field / footer with Page X of Y (1)
scheme.model_answer: The team should all use the same heading styles, so the headings look identical whoever wrote them. Then they can insert an automatic table of contents built from those styles and update it after each change. In the test-plan table they should switch on Repeat header rows so the column headings appear on all four pages, and give it a numbered caption so it can be referred to.

questions.title: Structuring the report
questions.text: A programmer is formatting a 40-page technical document for a new online shop. It has a title page, a contents page, five chapters and an appendix with a wide ERD.

parts.title: Heading styles
parts.text: Explain why the chapter titles should be formatted with heading styles.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): consistent; change all at once; automatic contents; navigation pane; StyleRef in header
scheme.model_answer: All chapter titles look the same, and the contents page can be generated automatically from them.

parts.title: Contents page
parts.text: Describe how the contents page can be created and kept correct as the document changes.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Insert an automatic table of contents (References → Table of Contents) based on heading styles (1)
- choose Update Table after editing so page numbers / headings are corrected (1)
scheme.model_answer: Insert an automatic table of contents from the References tab, built from the heading styles, and use Update Table after each change.

parts.title: Title page and appendix
parts.text: The title page must have no header, and the appendix must be printed in landscape. Explain how this can be done.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Different first page for the title page (1)
- section break before the appendix, landscape orientation for that section (1)
scheme.model_answer: Tick Different first page so the title page has no header, and insert a section break before the appendix so that section alone can be landscape.

parts.title: Footer fields
parts.text: State **two** fields that could be inserted in the footer.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): page number; number of pages; date; file name; author; StyleRef (chapter title)
scheme.model_answer: 1 Page number. 2 Total number of pages.

questions.title: Footnotes
questions.text: The analysis chapter uses information from interviews and from the Law on Personal Data. The programmer adds footnotes.

parts.title: Options
parts.text: State **two** footnote options the programmer can change.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): location; number format; start at; restart numbering; convert to endnotes
scheme.model_answer: 1 Number format. 2 Location — bottom of the page or end of the document.

parts.title: A source footnote
parts.text: Write a suitable footnote for the sentence *"Customers' personal data must be stored only with their consent."*, which is based on Article 8 of the Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan on Personal Data and its Protection.

scheme.mark_scheme: Names the law (1) and the article / source details (1)
scheme.model_answer: ¹ Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan "On Personal Data and its Protection", Article 8.

parts.title: Endnotes
parts.text: The client asks for all the sources to be listed together at the end of the document. Explain how this can be done quickly.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Convert footnotes to endnotes (References → Footnotes → Convert) (1)
- the notes are moved to the end of the document and renumbered automatically (1)
scheme.model_answer: Use the Convert option to change all footnotes into endnotes; they move to the end of the document and are renumbered automatically.

parts.title: Automatic numbering
parts.text: Explain **one** advantage of the automatic numbering of footnotes.

scheme.mark_scheme: Advantage (1) + explanation (1): renumbered when a note is added / deleted / moved, so numbers are always correct and in order
scheme.model_answer: When a footnote is inserted in the middle, all later footnotes are renumbered, so the numbers are always in the correct order.

questions.title: Formatting tables
questions.text: The testing chapter contains a test plan with 60 rows over three pages, and the design chapter contains six data-dictionary tables.

parts.title: Table tools
parts.text: Draw a line to link each table tool to its purpose.

right.text: Column headings shown on every page of the test plan
Each table gets an automatic number and title
All six data-dictionary tables look the same

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3, L4–R4. One mark per line.

parts.title: Captions
parts.text: Explain why captions should be inserted automatically for the six data-dictionary tables.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Automatic numbering / renumbering when tables are added (1)
- list of tables and cross-references update automatically (1)
scheme.model_answer: The tables are numbered automatically and renumbered if another table is added, and a list of tables can be generated.

parts.title: Cross-reference
parts.text: Explain what a cross-reference is and why it is useful in this document.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A field that refers to another item, e.g. "see Table 3 on page 12" (1)
- the number / page updates automatically when tables move (1)
scheme.model_answer: A cross-reference is a field such as "see Table 3 on page 12" that updates automatically if the table's number or page changes.

summary: Formatting project documentation professionally — styles and automatic tables of contents, sections and page layout, advanced headers and footers with fields, formatting and numbering footnotes and endnotes, and formatting tables with captions, header rows and cross-references.

theory.title: Why formatting matters in project documentation

blocks.content: Project documents are long (often 20–100 pages), are written by several people and change many times. Using the word processor's **automatic formatting tools** instead of formatting text by hand makes a document **consistent**, **easy to navigate** and **quick to update**.

blocks.title: Manual formatting vs automatic tools
rows: Make text bold and bigger each time
Type chapter names and page numbers
**Automatic table of contents** from heading styles
Type a number on each page
Type "1" and a note at the bottom

theory.title: Styles and the table of contents

blocks.content: A named set of formatting (font, size, colour, spacing, numbering) that can be applied to text in one click, e.g. **Heading 1**, **Heading 2**, **Normal**, **Caption**. Changing a style **updates all the text** that uses it.

items.title: Advantages of styles
items.content:
- **Consistent** look across the whole document and all authors.
- Change the design of every heading **at once** by modifying the style.
- Headings appear in the **navigation pane** — quick movement through a long document.
- Needed for an **automatic table of contents** and for chapter names in headers.

items.title: Automatic table of contents
items.content:
- Apply **Heading 1 / 2 / 3** to chapter and section titles.
- **References → Table of Contents**: the contents is built from the headings with page numbers and links.
- After editing, choose **Update Table** — new page numbers appear automatically.

blocks.title: Heading levels in a project report
blocks.content:
```text
1  Analysis                          <- Heading 1
1.1  Current system                  <- Heading 2
1.2  Requirements specification      <- Heading 2
2  Design                            <- Heading 1
2.1  Data dictionary                 <- Heading 2
2.1.1  Table Students                <- Heading 3
```
Use **multilevel list numbering** linked to the heading styles so the numbers (1, 1.1, 1.1.1) update when sections are added or moved.

blocks.title: Page layout settings
rows: Space for binding (wider inside margin); standard 2–2.5 cm
**Portrait** for text; **landscape** for wide tables or diagrams (ERD, Gantt chart)
Start each main chapter on a new page
Change orientation, margins, headers or page-number format for **part** of the document
Rarely in reports; sometimes in user leaflets
1.15–1.5 for readability; space after paragraphs instead of empty lines

blocks.title: Why section breaks are needed
blocks.content: A report has a title page (no header), a contents section numbered **i, ii, iii**, chapters numbered **1, 2, 3 …**, and an appendix with a **landscape** ERD. Each part is placed in its own **section** (Layout → Breaks → Section Break (Next Page)), and each section can have its own **orientation**, **header text** and **page-number format**.

blocks.title: Header and footer tools
rows: The title page has no header / footer
Page numbers on the outer edge, document title on even pages and chapter title on odd pages
Off = a new section can have **different** header text
1, 2, 3 / i, ii, iii / A, B, C; **start at** a chosen number
Page, NumPages ("Page 5 of 40"), Date, FileName, Author, **StyleRef** (shows the current Heading 1 automatically)
Distance of the header / footer from the page edge

blocks.title: A professional header and footer
blocks.content:
| Area | Left | Centre | Right |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Header** | Library Management System | | Design v2.0 — 14.10.2026 |
| **Footer** | Confidential — NIS Astana | Chapter 2: Design *(StyleRef field)* | Page 7 of 40 *(Page / NumPages fields)* |
Put left, centre and right text in a header using the **built-in centre and right tab stops**, or an invisible table with three cells, rather than spaces — spaces move when the font changes.

blocks.title: Footnote options (References → Footnotes dialog)
rows: Bottom of page / below text; end of document / end of section
Footnotes for explanations, endnotes for the reference list
Continuous / restart each section / restart each page
Continue numbering from a previous document
Change the style of the report quickly

items.title: Good practice for footnotes
items.content:
- Keep them **short** — one or two sentences.
- Place the reference mark **after the punctuation** at the end of the phrase.²
- Use a **consistent citation format** for sources (author, title, year, URL, date accessed).
- Use the **Footnote Text** style so all notes have the same font size (usually 1–2 points smaller than the main text).

items.title: Footnotes for sources in documentation
items.content:
- Requirements taken from an **interview** with the client: "¹ Interview with the head librarian, 03.10.2026."
- Data taken from a **standard** or law: "² Law of the RK on Personal Data, Article 8."
- A **definition** for users of a user guide: "³ A barcode scanner reads the black-and-white code on a book."

blocks.title: Table formatting tools
rows: Apply consistent borders, shading and fonts to all tables
Column headings visible on every page of a long table
Alternate shading makes long rows easier to follow
A heading spanning several columns; two columns under one heading
Columns fit the data and the page
Text left, numbers right or centred; vertical centring
**"Allow row to break across pages" — off**
A row is never split between two pages
Turn tab-separated data into a table

items.title: Captions and lists of tables
items.content:
- **References → Insert Caption** → "Table 1. Test plan for the login form". Table captions usually go **above** the table, figure captions **below** the figure.
- Captions are **numbered automatically** and renumber when tables are added.
- **Insert Table of Figures** creates a list of all tables / figures with page numbers.

items.title: Cross-references
items.content:
- **References → Cross-reference** inserts text such as "see **Table 4** on page **17**".
- The number and page **update automatically** (right-click → Update Field / press F9).

blocks.title: A well-formatted table
blocks.content:
**Table 4.** Test plan for the age field (valid range 11–18)

| No. | Test data | Type | Expected result | Actual result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 | Normal | Accepted | Accepted |
| 2 | 11 | Extreme | Accepted | Accepted |
| 3 | 19 | Erroneous | Error message | Error message |

*Numbered caption above the table; bold header row; numbers centred; consistent columns.*

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Explain why a programmer should use heading styles in the technical documentation. [2]**
All headings are formatted **consistently** and can be changed at once (1), and an **automatic table of contents** can be created from them / headings appear in the navigation pane (1).

**Q: The report's title page should have no header, and the appendix should be landscape. Explain how this can be done. [2]**
Use **Different first page** for the title page (1) and a **section break** before the appendix so that section can have **landscape orientation** (1).

**Q: Explain the advantage of inserting table captions with the Insert Caption tool. [2]**
Captions are **numbered automatically** and **renumbered** if tables are added or removed (1), and a **list of tables / cross-references** can be created and updated automatically (1).

**Q: State two options that can be changed for footnotes. [2]**
**Number format** (1, a, i, *) (1); **numbering restarts** each section / location — bottom of page or end of document (1).

- Making headings look like headings with bold and size instead of **heading styles** — the table of contents cannot be generated.
- Pressing Enter many times to reach a new page instead of inserting a **page break**.
- Typing "Table 3" by hand — the numbering breaks when a table is added.
- Forgetting to switch off **Link to previous**, so a change to one section's header changes all of them.
- Splitting a table row across two pages.

items: What is a style and why is it useful?
How is an automatic table of contents created and updated?
What is the difference between a page break and a section break?
Name four fields that can be inserted in a header or footer.
Name six tools for formatting tables.
What is a cross-reference and why does it update automatically?

topic_exam.instructions: Answer **all** questions. The number of marks is given in brackets [ ] at the end of each part. Total: 24 marks. Time: 25 minutes.
